title: Experts disagree on closeAbandonedBundles
context:
Chief architect: The three claims agree: a confirmed squash merge closes as done at once, anything without merge evidence keeps the 24h quiet wait, and the exact-match negatives ((#7660), #766 without parens, null pr.number) stay open. It is a pick only because the strict-match rule is a must-level security finding. The recommendation is the strict rule; the product-owner and qa claims are its outcome and its tests. Whether a confirmed merge may close a change that still has a stage running is a separate gap question below, so it is asked once there.

Target: closeAbandonedBundles
- security-auditor: a commit subject is text anyone with push rights can write, so the (#<pr.number>) match must read only the base branch, require a pr.number from the bundle's delivery record, and match the number exactly (so #76 never matches #766) before closing without the 24h quiet wait
- product-owner: a change whose PR is confirmed squash-merged on the base branch closes as done right away; changes with no merge evidence keep today's 24h quiet wait, so an unmerged change is never closed early
- qa-engineer: given delivery.json pr.number 766 and a base branch commit subject ending (#766), the bundle closes at once with status done; negatives that must stay open: (#7660), #766 without parens, pr.number null, and no matching commit within 24h quiet
